title.zh: 卷436 列傳二百二十三 沈桂芬 李鸿藻 翁同龢 孙毓汶
title.en: Volume 436 Biographies 223: Shen Guifen, Li Hongzao, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yuwen
title.raw: 卷436 列傳二百二十三 沈桂芬 李鸿藻 翁同龢 孙毓汶

sentences.zh: 沈桂芬，字經笙，順天宛平人，本籍江蘇吳江。

translations.literal: Shen Guifen, style name Jingsheng, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian; his original household registration was in Wujiang, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guifen, whose style was Jingsheng, came from Wanping in the Shuntian metropolitan district, though his ancestral home was Wujiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1847, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary academician, and received appointment as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，大考一等，擢庶子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, in the grand evaluation he ranked first class and was promoted to junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he took top honors in the triennial Hanlin review and was promoted to junior tutor in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to become a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先後典浙江、廣東鄉試，督陝甘學政，充會試副總裁。

translations.literal: In succession he presided over the provincial examinations of Zhejiang and Guangdong, supervised education in Shaanxi and Gansu, and served as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as chief examiner for the provincial examinations in Zhejiang and Guangdong, as education commissioner for Shaanxi and Gansu, and as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 晉禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to left vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，出署山西巡撫，明年，實授。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he went out to serve as acting governor of Shanxi; the next year he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was sent out to serve as acting governor of Shanxi, and the following year received the substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 連上移屯、練兵諸疏，並稱旨。

translations.literal: In succession he submitted memorials on colonization and troop training, all of which met with imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a series of memorials on land reclamation and military training, each of which won the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 桂芬以山西民食不敷，自洋藥弛禁，栽種罌粟，糧價踴增。

translations.literal: Guifen held that the people's food supply in Shanxi was insufficient; since the ban on foreign opium had been relaxed, poppies were cultivated and grain prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen argued that Shanxi's food supply was inadequate because, after the opium trade was legalized, farmers turned to poppy cultivation and grain prices shot up.

sentences.zh: 於是刊發條約，飭屬嚴禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he published and distributed regulations and ordered subordinates to enforce a strict ban.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore issued printed regulations and ordered his subordinates to enforce a strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 疏陳現辦情形，上韙之，頒行各省，著為令。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth the current measures; the throne approved them, promulgated them to all provinces, and made them standing orders.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he described his current measures; the emperor endorsed them, ordered their promulgation throughout the provinces, and made them standing policy.

sentences.zh: 旋丁母憂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office again to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 六年，起禮部右侍郎，充經筵講官，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was recalled as right vice minister of Rites, appointed lecturer at the imperial lecture sessions, and ordered to serve as a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was recalled as right vice minister of Rites, appointed lecturer at the emperor's study sessions, and named to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部，擢都察院左都御史，兼總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: He passed through the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel, was promoted to left censor-in-chief of the Censorate, and concurrently served as minister for the management of foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel in turn, was promoted to left censor-in-chief, and concurrently held office as minister for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of War and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of War and granted the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，以本官協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, with his present rank he was made associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875, while retaining his ministerial rank, he was appointed associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 京畿旱，編修何金壽援漢代天災策免三公為言，請責斥樞臣，諭交部議。

translations.literal: When the capital region suffered drought, compiler He Jinshou, citing the Han practice of dismissing the Three Excellencies on account of natural calamities, asked that the Grand Council ministers be held accountable; an edict ordered the matter referred to the relevant ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought in the capital region, compiler He Jinshou invoked the Han precedent of removing the Three Excellencies after natural disasters and called for the dismissal of the Grand Council ministers; the court ordered the relevant ministry to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 桂芬坐革職，特旨改為革職留任。

translations.literal: Guifen was sentenced to dismissal from office, but a special edict changed this to dismissal while retaining his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen was initially ordered dismissed, but a special edict commuted the penalty to dismissal while retaining his post.

sentences.zh: 旋復原官，充翰林院掌院學士，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to his former office, appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and advanced to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to office, appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and promoted to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 桂芬遇事持重，自文祥逝後，以諳究外情稱。

translations.literal: Guifen was deliberate in handling affairs; after Wen Xiang's death he was known for his thorough understanding of foreign conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen was cautious and measured in policy; after Wen Xiang's death he was regarded as the council member best versed in foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 日本之滅琉球也，廷論多主戰，桂芬獨言勞師海上，易損國威，力持不可。

translations.literal: When Japan extinguished Ryukyu, court opinion largely favored war; Guifen alone argued that exhausting troops at sea would easily damage national prestige, and he firmly held that war was inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan annexed Ryukyu, most at court favored war, but Guifen alone argued that dispatching forces across the sea would squander strength and damage national prestige, and he firmly opposed hostilities.

sentences.zh: 及與俄人議還伊犁，崇厚擅訂約，朝議紛然；

translations.literal: When negotiations with Russia over the return of Ili were undertaken, Chonghou concluded a treaty on his own authority, and court debate was vehement;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when negotiations with Russia over the return of Ili were under way, Chonghou signed a treaty on his own authority, provoking fierce debate at court;

sentences.zh: 桂芬委曲斡旋，易使往議，改約始定，而言者猶激論不已。

translations.literal: Guifen mediated with tact, replaced the envoy to negotiate anew, and only then was a revised treaty settled, yet critics still argued heatedly without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen worked behind the scenes to arrange a replacement envoy and secure a revised treaty, yet critics at court continued to argue without letup.

sentences.zh: 桂芬久臥病，六年，卒，年六十有四，贈太子太傅，諡文定。

translations.literal: Guifen had long been bedridden with illness; in the sixth year he died, aged sixty-four, and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen had been ill in bed for a long time; he died in 1880 at the age of sixty-four, and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 桂芬躬行謹飭，為軍機大臣十餘年，自奉若寒素，所處極湫隘，而未嘗以清節自矜，人以為難雲。

translations.literal: Guifen was scrupulous in personal conduct; for more than ten years as a Grand Council minister he lived as if in poverty, his dwelling extremely cramped and mean, yet he never prided himself on integrity, which people regarded as hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen was personally austere and upright; for more than a decade on the Grand Council he lived as modestly as a poor scholar in cramped quarters, yet never flaunted his integrity—a restraint people found remarkable.

sentences.zh: 李鴻藻，字蘭孫，直隸高陽人。

translations.literal: Li Hongzao, style name Lansun, was a native of Gaoyang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzao, whose style was Lansun, came from Gaoyang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1852, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary academician, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典山西鄉試，督河南學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shanxi provincial examination and supervised education in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for the Shanxi provincial examination and as education commissioner for Henan.

sentences.zh: 十年，上擇儒臣為皇子師，大學士彭蘊章以鴻藻應。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the emperor chose Confucian officials to serve as tutors to the princes; Grand Secretary Peng Yunzhang recommended Hongzao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 the emperor sought Confucian scholars to tutor the princes, and Grand Secretary Peng Yunzhang nominated Hongzao.

sentences.zh: 召來京，明年，特詔授大阿哥讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital; the next year a special edict appointed him tutor to the eldest imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to Beijing, and the following year a special edict named him tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 穆宗登極，皇太后懿旨命直弘德殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, the empress dowager's decree ordered him to serve in the Hall of the Cultivation of Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi ascended the throne, the empress dowager ordered him to attend at the Hall of the Cultivation of Virtue.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to expositor in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 署戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as acting left vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting left vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，命直軍機。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 五年，授禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed right vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he was appointed right vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，皇太后懿旨，援雍正、乾隆年大臣孫嘉淦等故事，命鴻藻開缺守孝，百日後仍授讀，兼參機務。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, the empress dowager's decree, citing the precedents of ministers such as Sun Jiagan in the Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns, ordered Hongzao to vacate his post to observe mourning, yet after one hundred days to resume tutoring and concurrently participate in council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the empress dowager cited precedents from the Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns—such as that of Sun Jiagan—and ordered Hongzao to leave office for mourning, but to resume tutoring after one hundred days while continuing to serve on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 並諭：「移孝作忠，勿以守禮固辭。

translations.literal: She also instructed: "Transform filial piety into loyalty; do not obstinately refuse on grounds of observing ritual."
translations.idiomatic: She also instructed him: "Let filial duty become loyalty to the throne; do not refuse on ritual grounds alone."

sentences.zh: 」鴻藻懇終制，不允。

translations.literal: Hongzao earnestly requested to complete the full mourning term; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao pleaded to observe the full three-year mourning period, but the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 倭仁等亦代為陳請，仍命恭親王傳諭慰勉。

translations.literal: Woren and others also submitted petitions on his behalf, yet the order still stood for Prince Gong to convey edicts of consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Woren and others petitioned on his behalf as well, but the court again had Prince Gong convey imperial words of consolation and urging.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻連疏稱疾，遂得賜告，卒終制始出。

translations.literal: Hongzao repeatedly memorialized claiming illness, and thus obtained leave; only when he had completed the full mourning did he emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao repeatedly memorialized citing illness and was granted leave; he did not return to duty until he had completed the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 七年，捻擾畿疆，鴻藻方里居，以各路統兵大員事權不一，疏請特派親王為大將軍，坐鎮京師，以固北路；

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Nian rebels harassed the capital region; Hongzao was then living at home and, because commanders of the various routes lacked unified authority, memorialized asking that a prince of the blood be specially appointed grand marshal to sit at Beijing and secure the northern route;
translations.idiomatic: In 1868, while the Nian rebels threatened the capital region and Hongzao was at home on leave, he memorialized that the field commanders lacked unified authority and asked that an imperial prince be appointed grand marshal at Beijing to secure the northern approaches;

sentences.zh: 左宗棠、李鴻章為參贊大臣，分扎保定、河間東西兩路，各率所部兵勇相機剿辦；

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang should serve as assistant grand marshals, stationed respectively on the eastern and western routes at Baoding and Hejian, each leading his own troops to suppress the rebels as circumstances allowed;
translations.idiomatic: with Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang as assistant grand marshals, stationed on the eastern and western routes at Baoding and Hejian respectively, each leading his own forces to pursue the rebels as opportunity allowed;

sentences.zh: 陳國瑞為幫辦軍務，專統一軍為游擊之師；

translations.literal: Chen Guorui should assist in military affairs, exclusively commanding one army as a mobile strike force;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guorui should assist in military affairs and command a separate mobile force;

sentences.zh: 直隸總督官文專顧省城，籌備諸軍餉需，以資接濟；

translations.literal: Zhili Governor-General Guanwen should attend solely to the provincial capital, preparing provisions and pay for the various armies to supply them;
translations.idiomatic: Zhili Governor-General Guanwen should remain at the provincial capital to organize supplies and pay for all the armies;

sentences.zh: 丁寶楨駐紮直、東交界，防賊東竄；

translations.literal: Ding Baozhen should be stationed at the Zhili-Shandong border to prevent the rebels from fleeing east;
translations.idiomatic: Ding Baozhen should be posted on the Zhili-Shandong border to block an eastern breakout;

sentences.zh: 李鶴年駐紮直、豫交界，防賊南竄；

translations.literal: Li Henian should be stationed at the Zhili-Henan border to prevent the rebels from fleeing south;
translations.idiomatic: Li Henian should be posted on the Zhili-Henan border to block a southern breakout;

sentences.zh: 直、晉交界，由左宗棠等分撥勁旅扼要駐紮；

translations.literal: At the Zhili-Shanxi border, Zuo Zongtang and others should allocate crack troops to hold key positions;
translations.idiomatic: at the Zhili-Shanxi border, Zuo Zongtang and others should deploy elite troops at strategic points;

sentences.zh: 並請敕下各該大臣和衷商辦，迅奏膚功。

translations.literal: He also asked that an edict be issued ordering all these ministers to deliberate in harmony and quickly report complete victory.
translations.idiomatic: and he asked that an edict direct all these officials to cooperate harmoniously and report swift success.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上遂命各路統兵大臣均歸恭親王節制。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor thereupon ordered all field commanders to come under Prince Gong's command.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor ordered all field commanders placed under Prince Gong's overall command.

sentences.zh: 旋起禮部左侍郎，仍直弘德殿及軍機如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as left vice minister of Rites and continued to serve in the Hall of Cultivation of Virtue and on the Grand Council as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as left vice minister of Rites and resumed his posts at the imperial study hall and on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢都察院左都御史，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to left censor-in-chief and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he was promoted to left censor-in-chief and granted the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時有修葺圓明園之旨，朝臣同起力爭。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict to repair the Old Summer Palace, and court officials rose together in strenuous opposition.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was issued to restore the Old Summer Palace, officials at court united in vigorous opposition.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻亦言：「粵、捻初平，回氛方熾，宜培養元氣，以固根本。

translations.literal: Hongzao also said: "The Guangdong rebels and the Nian have only just been pacified, while Muslim unrest is still fierce; the state should nurture its vital energies to strengthen its foundations."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao also argued: "The Taiping and Nian rebellions have only just ended and Muslim unrest is still raging; the court should conserve its strength and shore up the foundations of rule."

sentences.zh: 不應虛糜帑糈，為此不急之務。

translations.literal: It should not squander treasury funds on such non-urgent business.
translations.idiomatic: It should not squander public funds on so unnecessary a project.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The project was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上有疾，命代批答章奏；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor fell ill and ordered him to draft replies to memorials on his behalf;
translations.idiomatic: In 1874 the emperor fell ill and ordered Hongzao to draft memorial replies on his behalf;

sentences.zh: 旋崩，自劾輔導無狀，罷弘德殿行走。

translations.literal: The emperor soon died; Hongzao impeached himself for failure in tutoring, and was removed from attendance at the Hall of Cultivation of Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor soon died; Hongzao submitted a self-accusation for failing in his tutelage and was dismissed from the imperial study hall.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，命兼總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he was ordered concurrently to serve at the Yamen for the management of foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he was ordered concurrently to serve at the foreign affairs office.

sentences.zh: 尋丁本生母憂，服闋，起故官，以兵部尚書協辦大學士，調吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his birth mother; when the mourning ended he was recalled to his former office, made associate grand secretary while minister of War, and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon mourned his birth mother; after the mourning period he was recalled, appointed associate grand secretary while serving as minister of War, and then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時崇厚與俄擅定伊犁約，鴻藻堅持不可，爭於廷。

translations.literal: At that time Chonghou had on his own authority concluded the Ili treaty with Russia; Hongzao firmly held that it was unacceptable and argued in court.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghou signed the Ili treaty with Russia on his own authority, Hongzao firmly opposed it and debated the matter at court.

sentences.zh: 卒治崇厚罪，議改約。

translations.literal: In the end Chonghou was punished, and a revised treaty was negotiated.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou was eventually punished and negotiations for a revised treaty were undertaken.

sentences.zh: 及法越啟釁，言路愈奮發，劾罷樞臣。

translations.literal: When hostilities opened between France and Vietnam, the censorial remonstrators grew ever more vehement and impeached the Grand Council ministers until they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French conflict erupted, memorialists grew ever bolder and impeached the Grand Council ministers until they were removed.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻謫遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: Hongzao was demoted and transferred to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao was demoted to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後復累遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was again promoted by stages to minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted again by stages to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，河決鄭州，上命鴻藻馳往督辦。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Yellow River burst its banks at Zhengzhou; the emperor ordered Hongzao to proceed posthaste to supervise repairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 the Yellow River broke through its dikes at Zhengzhou, and the emperor ordered Hongzao to hurry there to supervise the repair work.

sentences.zh: 先是河道總督李鶴年、河南巡撫倪文蔚議於西壩興工，鴻藻至，仍之。

translations.literal: Earlier the director-general of waterways Li Henian and Henan Governor Ni Wenwei had proposed works at the western embankment; when Hongzao arrived, he continued the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Director-General of Waterways Li Henian and Henan Governor Ni Wenwei had proposed work on the western embankment; when Hongzao arrived, he carried the plan forward.

sentences.zh: 又續興東壩工。

translations.literal: He also continued work on the eastern embankment.
translations.idiomatic: He also undertook continued work on the eastern embankment.

sentences.zh: 疊遇奇險，皆力為固守。

translations.literal: Repeatedly encountering extraordinary dangers, he exerted himself to hold firm on all occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Despite repeated crises he threw all his strength into holding the works firm.

sentences.zh: 會伏秋汛至，西壩失事，請暫停工。

translations.literal: When the midsummer and autumn flood season arrived, the western embankment failed; he requested a temporary halt to work.
translations.idiomatic: When the summer and autumn flood season arrived, the western embankment gave way, and he requested a temporary suspension of work.

sentences.zh: 上以鴻藻督率無方，革職留任；

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Hongzao had lacked proper direction, ordered dismissal from office while retaining his duties;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Hongzao for ineffective supervision and ordered him dismissed while retaining his post;

sentences.zh: 並奪李鶴年河道總督，命鴻藻暫行署理。

translations.literal: Li Henian was also stripped of the director-generalship of waterways, and Hongzao was ordered temporarily to act in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Li Henian was also removed as director-general of waterways, and Hongzao was ordered to act in his place temporarily.

sentences.zh: 尋回京，復以禮部具奏典禮漏繕簽改日期，再議革職，上特寬免。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to the capital; again the Ministry of Rites reported that in a ceremonial document the date on the cover slip had been wrongly altered, and dismissal was again proposed, but the emperor specially granted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Beijing; the Ministry of Rites then reported that a ceremonial document had a wrongly altered date on its cover slip, and dismissal was proposed again, but the emperor specially spared him.

sentences.zh: 大婚禮成，復原官。

translations.literal: When the grand wedding ceremony was completed, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand imperial wedding was completed, he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日韓事棘，命鴻藻商辦軍務，再授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, as affairs between Japan and Korea grew critical, Hongzao was ordered to assist in military affairs and was again appointed a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, as the Japan-Korea crisis intensified, Hongzao was ordered to assist in military affairs and was again appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 與翁同龢皆主戰，並爭和約，卒不能阻。

translations.literal: He and Weng Tonghe both favored war and together opposed the peace treaty, but in the end could not prevent it.
translations.idiomatic: He and Weng Tonghe both favored war and together opposed the peace treaty, but in the end could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 旋以禮部尚書協辦大學士，調吏部。

translations.literal: Soon, as minister of Rites, he was made associate grand secretary and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed associate grand secretary while serving as minister of Rites, and then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歷蒙頒賞書畫及諸上方珍物。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received imperial gifts of paintings, calligraphy, and various precious objects from the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He received repeated imperial gifts of paintings, calligraphy, and other precious objects from the palace stores.

sentences.zh: 充鄉試、會試、殿試等閱卷大臣。

translations.literal: He served as grading officer for the provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief grading officer for the provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以病乞假，疾篤，賞給藥餌，命御醫往視。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, citing illness, he requested leave; when his illness grew grave, medicines were bestowed and an imperial physician was sent to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he requested leave on grounds of illness; when his condition worsened, the court sent medicines and dispatched an imperial physician to attend him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有八。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 遺疏入，上震悼，予諡文正，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: When his final memorial was submitted, the emperor was deeply shaken and grieved; he was granted the posthumous title Wenzheng and posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his death memorial reached the throne, the emperor was deeply grieved; he was granted the posthumous title Wenzheng and posthumously honored as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子焜瀛、煜瀛，均賞給郎中。

translations.literal: His sons Kunying and Yuying were both granted the rank of director in a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kunying and Yuying were both granted the rank of director in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻性至孝，為學守程硃，務實踐，持躬儉約。

translations.literal: Hongzao was by nature profoundly filial; in learning he adhered to the Cheng-Zhu school, stressed practical conduct, and was frugal in personal bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao was profoundly filial by nature; in scholarship he followed the Cheng-Zhu school, emphasized practical conduct, and lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 傅穆宗十餘年，盡心啟沃。

translations.literal: He tutored Emperor Muzong for more than ten years and devoted his whole heart to instruction and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He tutored Emperor Tongzhi for more than a decade and devoted himself wholeheartedly to the young emperor's instruction.

sentences.zh: 一日，穆宗學書，故為戲筆。

translations.literal: One day, while Emperor Muzong was practicing calligraphy, he deliberately wrote in a playful hand.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while the emperor was practicing calligraphy, he deliberately wrote in a careless, playful hand.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻立前捧上手曰：「皇上心不靜，請少息。

translations.literal: Hongzao stepped forward, took the emperor's hand in both of his, and said: "Your Majesty's mind is not calm; please rest a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao stepped forward, took the emperor's hand in both of his, and said, "Your Majesty's mind is unsettled; please pause for a moment."

sentences.zh: 」穆宗改容謝之。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong changed his expression and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately composed his manner and apologized.

sentences.zh: 其在樞府，獨守正持大體。

translations.literal: In the Grand Council he alone upheld rectitude and grasped the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Council he alone upheld principle and kept sight of the larger interests of state.

sentences.zh: 御史王鵬運諫止修頤和園，幾獲重譴，鴻藻力解之，得免。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Pengyun memorialized to stop repairs to the Summer Palace and nearly incurred severe punishment; Hongzao strongly interceded for him, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Wang Pengyun memorialized against restoring the Summer Palace and nearly incurred severe punishment, Hongzao intervened forcefully on his behalf and secured his pardon.

sentences.zh: 德宗間日一往頤和園侍起居，時留駐蹕。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong went every other day to the Summer Palace to attend the empress dowager's daily routine, and at times remained there in residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangxu visited the Summer Palace every other day to attend the empress dowager, and sometimes stayed there for extended periods.

sentences.zh: 言官有言其不便者，太后大怒，欲黜之，鴻藻謂如此必失天下臣民之望，乃止。

translations.literal: When remonstrating officials spoke of the inconvenience of this, the empress dowager was greatly angered and wished to dismiss them; Hongzao said that to do so would surely lose the hope of all officials and people under Heaven, and she desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When memorialists criticized the arrangement, the empress dowager was furious and wished to dismiss them; Hongzao warned that doing so would forfeit the goodwill of officials and subjects throughout the empire, and she relented.

sentences.zh: 所薦引多端士。

translations.literal: Those he recommended and advanced were mostly men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended and advanced were mostly men of genuine talent.

sentences.zh: 朝列有清望者，率倚以為重，然亦不免被劫持雲。

translations.literal: Officials at court with pure reputation generally relied on him as a weighty figure, yet he also could not avoid being manipulated, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at court with reputations for integrity generally looked to him as their anchor, yet he too could not entirely escape being manipulated, it was said.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢，字叔平，江蘇常熟人，大學士心存子。

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe, style name Shuping, was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu, and the son of Grand Secretary Weng Xincun.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe, whose style was Shuping, came from Changshu in Jiangsu and was the son of Grand Secretary Weng Xincun.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he ranked first in the first class of jinshi graduates and was appointed drafting compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he took first place among the jinshi graduates and was appointed drafting compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 八年，典試陝甘，旋授陝西學政，乞病回京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu examination, was soon appointed education commissioner of Shaanxi, and requested leave for illness and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he served as chief examiner for Shaanxi and Gansu, was soon appointed education commissioner of Shaanxi, then requested leave on grounds of illness and returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢贊善。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to tutor in the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to tutor in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 典山西試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shanxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for the Shanxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，服闋，轉中允。

translations.literal: When his father died he returned home; when mourning ended, he was transferred to junior supervisor of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he returned to office and was transferred to junior supervisor of instruction.

sentences.zh: 命在弘德殿行走，五日一進講，於簾前說治平寶鑑，兩宮皇太后嘉之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to attend at the Hall of the Cultivation of Virtue, lecturing once every five days; before the screen he expounded the Mirror of Governance and Peace, and both empress dowagers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to attend at the Hall of the Cultivation of Virtue, lecturing every five days; before the screen he expounded the Mirror of Governance and Peace, and both empress dowagers commended him.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母憂服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 同龢居講席，每以憂勤惕厲，啟沃聖心。

translations.literal: At his lectern Tonghe always urged vigilance, diligence, and self-restraint to nourish the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In the lecture hall Tonghe always urged vigilance, diligence, and restraint to guide the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 當八年武英殿之災也，恭錄康熙、嘉慶兩次遇災修省聖訓進禦，疏言：「變不虛生，遇災而懼。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Martial Glory burned in the eighth year, he respectfully transcribed the imperial admonitions on self-examination from the Kangxi and Jiaqing reigns after similar disasters and presented them to the throne, memorializing: "Calamities do not arise without cause; one should fear when meeting disaster."
translations.idiomatic: When the Hall of Martial Glory burned in 1869, he transcribed the Kangxi and Jiaqing emperors' admonitions on self-examination after disasters and presented them to the throne, memorializing: "Calamities do not arise without cause; one must tremble when disaster strikes."

sentences.zh: 宜停不急之工，惜無名之費。

translations.literal: Non-urgent works should be halted and pointless expenditures curtailed.
translations.idiomatic: The court should halt non-urgent projects and cut wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 開直臣忠諫之路，杜小人幸進之門。

translations.literal: Open the path for loyal remonstrance by upright ministers and block the gate through which petty men advance by favor.
translations.idiomatic: Open the way for upright ministers to speak frankly, and shut the door to petty men who advance by flattery.

sentences.zh: 」上覽奏動容。

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial, his expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, the emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 又圓明園方興工，商人李光昭矇報木價，為李鴻章所劾論罪。

translations.literal: Work on the Old Summer Palace was meanwhile under way; the merchant Li Guangzhao had fraudulently reported timber prices and was impeached and punished by Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile work on the Old Summer Palace had begun; merchant Li Guangzhao had fraudulently inflated timber prices and was impeached and punished by Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多執此入諫，恭親王等尤力諍，上不懌。

translations.literal: Many court officials seized on this to remonstrate; Prince Gong and others argued especially forcefully, and the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials seized on the case to remonstrate; Prince Gong and others argued especially forcefully, to the emperor's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 同龢面陳江南輿論，中外人心惶惑，請聖意先定，待時興修。

translations.literal: Tonghe stated in person the opinion in Jiangnan and the anxiety at home and abroad, asking that the imperial mind be settled first and reconstruction wait for a proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe stated in person the public mood in Jiangnan and the anxiety throughout the empire, asking that the emperor settle his mind first and postpone reconstruction until a better time.

sentences.zh: 乃議定停園工，並有停工程、罷浮費、求直言之諭。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was decided to halt work on the gardens, and edicts were issued to stop projects, abolish wasteful spending, and seek frank counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The court then decided to halt the garden works and issued edicts to stop projects, cut wasteful spending, and invite frank memorials.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，署刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he served as acting right vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he served as acting right vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，上典學毓慶宮，命授讀，再辭，不允。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year the emperor began his studies at the Palace of Accumulated Happiness and was ordered to appoint Tonghe as tutor; he declined twice but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In April of the following year the emperor began his studies at the Palace of Accumulated Happiness and ordered Tonghe appointed as tutor; Tonghe declined twice but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 旋遷戶部，充經筵講官，晉都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Revenue, appointed lecturer at the imperial lecture sessions, and advanced to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, appointed lecturer at the imperial study sessions, and promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of Punishments and then to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of Punishments and then to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 六年，廷臣爭俄約久不決，懿旨派惇親王、醇親王及同龢與潘祖廕每日在南書房看摺件電報，擬片進呈取進止，至俄約改定始止。

translations.literal: In the sixth year court officials disputed the Russian treaty for a long time without resolution; an empress dowager decree assigned Prince Dun, Prince Chun, Tonghe, and Pan Zuyin to review memorials and telegrams daily in the Southern Study, draft rescripts for imperial decision, until the Russian treaty was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880 court debate over the Russian treaty dragged on; an empress dowager decree assigned Prince Dun, Prince Chun, Tonghe, and Pan Zuyin to review memorials and telegrams daily in the Southern Study and draft rescripts for imperial approval until the treaty was revised.

sentences.zh: 八年，命充軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十年，法越事起，同龢主一面進兵，一面與議，庶有所備。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the Franco-Vietnamese conflict arose, Tonghe held that troops should advance while negotiations proceeded, so that the state might be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, when the Sino-French conflict erupted, Tonghe argued for advancing troops while negotiating, so the court would not be caught unprepared.

sentences.zh: 又言劉永福不足恃，非增重兵出關不可。

translations.literal: He also said that Liu Yongfu could not be relied upon and that substantial reinforcements must be sent beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Liu Yongfu could not be relied upon and that substantial reinforcements must be sent beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 旋與軍機王大臣同罷，仍直毓慶宮。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed along with the Wang princes on the Grand Council, but continued to attend at the Palace of Accumulated Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed from the Grand Council along with the Wang princes, but continued to attend at the Palace of Accumulated Happiness.

sentences.zh: 前後充會試總裁、順天鄉試考官，兩蒙賜「壽」，加太子太保，賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: Before and after he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination and examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination, twice received the character shou as an imperial gift, was given the additional title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and was granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as chief examiner of the metropolitan and Shuntian provincial examinations, twice received the imperial gift of the character shou, was granted Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and received double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 嘗請假修墓，傳旨海上風險，命馳驛回京，恩眷甚篤。

translations.literal: Once, when he requested leave to repair his family tombs, an edict noted the dangers at sea and ordered him to return to the capital by courier post; imperial favor was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he requested leave to repair his family tombs, an edict cited the dangers at sea and ordered him to return to Beijing by courier post—a mark of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 二十年，再授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was again appointed a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was again appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 懿旨命撤講，上請如故。

translations.literal: An empress dowager decree ordered that lectures be withdrawn; the emperor asked that they continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: An empress dowager decree ordered his lectures withdrawn; the emperor asked that they continue unchanged.

sentences.zh: 同龢善伺上意，得遇事進言。

translations.literal: Tonghe was skilled at discerning the emperor's mind and thus could offer counsel when matters arose.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe was skilled at reading the emperor's mind and could offer counsel whenever the occasion arose.

sentences.zh: 上親政久，英爽非復常度，剖決精當。

translations.literal: The emperor had long ruled in person; his keenness was no longer ordinary, and his decisions were precise and apt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ruled in person for some time; his judgment was sharper than before and his decisions precise.

sentences.zh: 每事必問同龢，眷倚尤重。

translations.literal: On every matter he would consult Tonghe, and his reliance on him was especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: On every matter he consulted Tonghe, and his reliance on him was especially great.

sentences.zh: 時日韓起釁，同龢與李鴻藻主戰，孫毓汶、徐用儀主和。

translations.literal: At that time conflict arose between Japan and Korea; Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored war, while Sun Yuwen and Xu Yongyi favored peace.
translations.idiomatic: When conflict erupted between Japan and Korea, Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored war, while Sun Yuwen and Xu Yongyi favored peace.

sentences.zh: 會海陸軍皆敗，懿旨命赴天津傳諭李鴻章詰責之，同龢並言太后意決不即和。

translations.literal: When both the navy and army were defeated, an empress dowager decree ordered Tonghe to go to Tianjin to convey imperial rebuke to Li Hongzhang; Tonghe also stated that the empress dowager was resolved not to make peace immediately.
translations.idiomatic: When both navy and army were defeated, an empress dowager decree sent Tonghe to Tianjin to rebuke Li Hongzhang; Tonghe also reported that the empress dowager was resolved not to make peace immediately.

sentences.zh: 歸薦唐仁廉忠赤可用，請設巡防處籌辦團防。

translations.literal: On his return he recommended Tang Renlian as loyal and usable, and asked that a patrol defense office be established to organize local militia defense.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he recommended Tang Renlian as loyal and capable, and proposed establishing a patrol defense office to organize local militia.

sentences.zh: 於是命恭親王督辦軍務，同龢、鴻藻等會商辦理。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Gong was ordered to supervise military affairs, with Tonghe, Hongzao, and others to consult and manage together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong was then ordered to supervise military affairs, with Tonghe, Hongzao, and others to consult and manage together.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問諸臣：「時事至此，和戰皆無可恃！

translations.literal: The emperor once asked his ministers: "Affairs have come to this pass—neither peace nor war can be relied upon!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked his ministers: "Affairs have come to this pass—neither peace nor war offers any security!"

sentences.zh: 」言及宗社，聲淚並發。

translations.literal: When he spoke of the altars of state, his voice and tears flowed together.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of the fate of the dynasty, his voice broke and tears fell together.

sentences.zh: 及和議起，同龢與鴻藻力爭改約稿，並陳：「寧增賠款，必不可割地。

translations.literal: When peace negotiations began, Tonghe and Hongzao strove to alter the draft treaty and jointly stated: "Better to increase indemnity than to cede territory."
translations.idiomatic: When peace negotiations began, Tonghe and Hongzao fought to revise the draft treaty and jointly declared: "Better to increase the indemnity than to cede territory."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「台灣去，則人心皆去。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If Taiwan is lost, the hearts of all will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If Taiwan is lost, the hearts of the people will be lost with it."

sentences.zh: 朕何以為天下主？

translations.literal: How can I remain sovereign over all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: How then can I remain sovereign over the empire?

sentences.zh: 」毓汶以前敵屢敗對，上責以賞罰不嚴，故至於此。

translations.literal: Yuwen replied by citing repeated defeats of our forces; the emperor blamed lax rewards and punishments for bringing matters to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen replied by citing repeated defeats; the emperor blamed lax discipline in rewards and punishments for bringing matters to this pass.

sentences.zh: 諸臣皆引咎。

translations.literal: All the ministers accepted blame.
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers accepted the blame.

sentences.zh: 上以和約事徘徊不能決，天顏憔悴。

translations.literal: The emperor wavered over the peace treaty, unable to decide; his countenance was haggard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wavered over the peace treaty, unable to decide; his face was haggard with care.

sentences.zh: 同龢以俄、英、德三國謀阻割地，請展期換約，以待轉圜。

translations.literal: Tonghe, because Russia, Britain, and Germany were seeking to block the cession of territory, asked to extend the deadline for exchanging the treaty to await a turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe noted that Russia, Britain, and Germany were seeking to block territorial cession and asked to extend the deadline for exchanging the treaty to await a turn of events.

sentences.zh: 與毓汶等執爭，終不可挽，和約遂定。

translations.literal: He argued fiercely with Yuwen and others, but in the end could not prevail, and the peace treaty was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He argued fiercely with Yuwen and others but could not prevail, and the peace treaty was settled.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: The next year he was concurrently appointed minister for foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was concurrently appointed minister for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, as minister of Revenue he was made associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897, while serving as minister of Revenue, he was appointed associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，上初召用主事康有為，議行新政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the emperor first summoned and employed the principal clerk Kang Youwei and discussed implementing the New Policies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 the emperor first summoned Principal Clerk Kang Youwei and discussed implementing the New Policies.

sentences.zh: 四月，硃諭：「協辦大學士翁同龢近來辦事多不允協，以致眾論不服，屢經有人參奏。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict in vermilion ink stated: "Associate Grand Secretary Weng Tonghe of late has handled affairs in ways that often fail to win agreement, so that public opinion is dissatisfied and he has repeatedly been impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month a vermilion edict stated: "Associate Grand Secretary Weng Tonghe has of late handled affairs in ways that often fail to win agreement, provoking dissatisfaction and repeated impeachments.

sentences.zh: 且每於召對時諮詢事件，任意可否，喜怒見於詞色，漸露攬權狂悖情狀，斷難勝樞機之任。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever he was summoned for audience and questioned about affairs, he arbitrarily assented or dissented; joy and anger showed in his words and expression, gradually revealing a grasping, arrogant disposition; he clearly cannot bear the duties of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whenever summoned to audience he arbitrarily assented or dissented; joy and anger showed in his words and bearing, gradually revealing grasping, arrogant conduct; he clearly cannot bear Grand Council responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 本應查明究辦，予以重懲；

translations.literal: He ought to be investigated and severely punished;
translations.idiomatic: He ought to be investigated and severely punished;

sentences.zh: 姑念其在毓慶宮行走有年，不忍遽加嚴譴。

translations.literal: yet considering his years of attendance at the Palace of Accumulated Happiness, the court is unwilling to impose harsh censure immediately.
translations.idiomatic: yet considering his years of service at the Palace of Accumulated Happiness, the court is unwilling to impose harsh punishment immediately.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢著即開缺回籍，以示保全。

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe is forthwith to vacate his post and return to his native place, as a mark of lenient preservation."
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe is forthwith to vacate his post and return home, as an act of lenient preservation."

sentences.zh: 」八月，政變作，太后復訓政。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the coup occurred and the empress dowager resumed regency.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the coup occurred and the empress dowager resumed the regency.

sentences.zh: 十月，又奉硃諭：「翁同龢授讀以來，輔導無方，往往巧藉事端，刺探朕意。

translations.literal: In the tenth month another vermilion edict stated: "Since Weng Tonghe undertook instruction, his guidance has been inept; he often cleverly used pretexts to probe the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month another vermilion edict stated: "Since undertaking the emperor's instruction, Weng Tonghe's guidance has been inept; he often cleverly used pretexts to probe the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 至甲午年中東之役，信口侈陳，任意慫恿。

translations.literal: As for the Sino-Japanese war in the jiawu year, he spoke extravagantly and recklessly urged action.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sino-Japanese war of 1894 he spoke recklessly and urged rash action.

sentences.zh: 辦理諸務，種種乖謬，以致不可收拾。

translations.literal: In handling various affairs he committed error after error, until matters became irremediable.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he committed error after error until matters became irremediable.

sentences.zh: 今春力陳變法，濫保非人，罪無可逭。

translations.literal: This spring he forcefully advocated reform and recklessly recommended unworthy men; his guilt admits no excuse.
translations.idiomatic: This spring he forcefully advocated reform and recklessly recommended unworthy men; his guilt admits no excuse.

sentences.zh: 事後追維，深堪痛恨！

translations.literal: Looking back afterward, the court is deeply grieved and resentful!
translations.idiomatic: Looking back afterward, the court is deeply grieved and resentful!

sentences.zh: 前令其開缺回籍，實不足以蔽辜，翁同龢著革職，永不敘用，交地方官嚴加管束。

translations.literal: Previously ordering him to vacate his post and return home was truly insufficient to cover his guilt; Weng Tonghe is dismissed from office, never to be employed again, and placed under strict supervision by local officials."
translations.idiomatic: Previously ordering him home was insufficient to answer his guilt; Weng Tonghe is dismissed from office, never to be employed again, and placed under strict supervision by local officials."

sentences.zh: 」三十年，卒於家，年七十有五。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died at home, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In 1904 he died at home at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，詔復原官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong an edict restored his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909 an edict restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 後追諡文恭。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted the title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously granted the title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 同龢久侍講幃，參機務，遇事專斷。

translations.literal: Tonghe long attended the lecture curtain and participated in confidential affairs, deciding matters on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe long served as imperial tutor and participated in confidential affairs, often deciding matters on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 與左右時有爭執，群責怙權。

translations.literal: He frequently quarreled with those around him, and the group blamed him for monopolizing power.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently quarreled with colleagues, and many blamed him for monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 晚遭讒沮，幾獲不測，遂斥逐以終。

translations.literal: In his later years he suffered slander and nearly met with disaster, ending his career in dismissal and exile.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he suffered slander and nearly met disaster, ending in dismissal and exile.

sentences.zh: 著有瓶廬詩稿八卷、文稿二十卷。

translations.literal: He authored eight juan of Poetic Drafts from the Bottle Studio and twenty juan of prose drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He authored eight juan of Poetic Drafts from the Bottle Studio and twenty juan of prose drafts.

sentences.zh: 其書法自成一家，尤為世所宗雲。

translations.literal: His calligraphy formed a school of its own and was especially revered by the world, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy formed a school of its own and was especially revered, it is said.

sentences.zh: 孫毓汶，字萊山，山東濟寧州人，尚書瑞珍子。

translations.literal: Sun Yuwen, style name Laishan, was a native of Jining prefecture in Shandong, and the son of Minister Sun Ruizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuwen, whose style was Laishan, came from Jining prefecture in Shandong and was the son of Minister Sun Ruizhen.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，以一甲二名進士授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, as second in the first class of jinshi graduates, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, as second-place finisher among the jinshi graduates, he was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十年，以在籍辦團抗捐被劾，革職遣戍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, for organizing local militia at home and resisting levies, he was impeached, dismissed from office, and sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, for organizing local militia at home and resisting tax levies, he was impeached, dismissed, and sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 恭親王以毓汶世受國恩，首抗捐餉，深惡之。

translations.literal: Prince Gong, because Yuwen's family had long received imperial grace yet he was foremost in resisting levies, deeply detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong deeply detested him because his family had long received imperial favor yet he was foremost in resisting levies.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以輸餉復原官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, by contributing funds for military pay he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, by contributing funds for military pay, he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 五年，大考一等一名，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, ranking first in the grand evaluation, he was promoted to supervising lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he took first place in the Hanlin grand evaluation and was promoted to supervising lecturer.

sentences.zh: 先後典四川鄉試，督福建學政。

translations.literal: In succession he presided over the Sichuan provincial examination and supervised education in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He successively presided over the Sichuan provincial examination and served as education commissioner for Fujian.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 尋遷詹事，視學安徽。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to junior tutor of the heir apparent and inspected education in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent and sent to inspect education in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 擢內閣學士，授工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat and appointed left vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to bachelor of the Grand Secretariat and appointed left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十年，命赴江南等省按事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to proceed to Jiangnan and other provinces to investigate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he was ordered to Jiangnan and other provinces to investigate affairs.

sentences.zh: 時法越事起，毓汶以習於醇親王，漸與聞機要。

translations.literal: At that time the Franco-Vietnamese conflict had arisen; Yuwen, being familiar with Prince Chun, gradually came to hear confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French conflict erupted, Yuwen, being close to Prince Chun, gradually gained access to confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 適奉硃諭盡罷軍機王大臣，毓汶還，遂命入直軍機，兼總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: Just then a vermilion edict dismissed all the Wang princes on the Grand Council; when Yuwen returned, he was ordered to serve on the council and concurrently as minister for foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a vermilion edict dismissed all the Wang princes on the Grand Council; when Yuwen returned, he was appointed to the council and concurrently as minister for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 時當國益厭言路紛囂，出張佩綸等會辦南北洋、閩海軍務，餘亦因事先後去之，風氣為之一變。

translations.literal: At that time those in power increasingly wearied of the clamor of remonstrating officials; Zhang Peilun and others were sent to manage naval affairs on the northern and southern coasts and in Fujian, and the rest also left one after another on various assignments, and the atmosphere changed markedly.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power increasingly wearied of remonstrating officials; Zhang Peilun and others were sent to manage coastal naval affairs, and others left on various assignments, markedly changing the political atmosphere.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢刑部尚書，尋調兵部，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to minister of Punishments, soon transferred to War, and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 he was promoted to minister of Punishments, soon transferred to War, and granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歷典會試、順天鄉試，賞黃馬褂、雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: He presided over the metropolitan and Shuntian provincial examinations in succession and was granted a yellow riding jacket, double-eyed peacock feathers, and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the metropolitan and Shuntian examinations in succession and received a yellow riding jacket, double-eyed peacock feathers, and a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日媾和，李鴻章遣人齎約至。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year China and Japan made peace; Li Hongzhang sent someone bearing the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 China and Japan made peace; Li Hongzhang sent an envoy bearing the treaty.

sentences.zh: 廷臣章奏凡百上，皆斥和非計。

translations.literal: Court memorials numbering in the hundreds were submitted, all denouncing peace as a mistaken policy.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of memorials reached court, all denouncing peace as mistaken policy.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢、李鴻藻主緩，俄、法、德三國亦請毋遽換約。

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored delay; Russia, France, and Germany also asked that the treaty not be exchanged hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe and Li Hongzao favored delay; Russia, France, and Germany also asked that the treaty not be exchanged hastily.

sentences.zh: 毓汶素與鴻章相結納，力言戰不可恃，亟請署，上為流涕書之，和約遂成。

translations.literal: Yuwen had long been allied with Li Hongzhang; he strongly argued that war could not be relied upon and urgently asked for signature; the emperor wept as he wrote his approval, and the peace treaty was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen had long been allied with Li Hongzhang; he argued that war could not be relied upon and urgently pressed for signature; the emperor wept as he approved it, and the peace treaty was concluded.

sentences.zh: 明年，稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: The next year, citing illness, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he requested retirement on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，予諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died and was granted the posthumous title Wenkai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1899 he died and was granted the posthumous title Wenkai.

sentences.zh: 毓汶權奇饒智略，直軍機逾十年。

translations.literal: Yuwen was resourceful and possessed abundant stratagems; he served on the Grand Council for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen was resourceful and possessed abundant stratagems; he served on the Grand Council for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 初，醇親王以尊親參機密，不常入直，疏牘日送邸閱，謂之「過府」。

translations.literal: At first Prince Chun, as an imperial kinsman participating in confidential affairs, did not regularly attend council sessions; documents were sent daily to his residence for review, called "passing through the mansion."
translations.idiomatic: At first Prince Chun, as an imperial kinsman in confidential affairs, did not regularly attend council; documents were sent daily to his residence for review, called "passing through the mansion."

sentences.zh: 諭旨陳奏，皆毓汶為傳達。

translations.literal: Imperial edicts and memorial presentations were all conveyed by Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts and memorial presentations were all conveyed through Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 同列或不得預聞，故其權特重雲。

translations.literal: Colleagues sometimes could not learn of matters beforehand, and therefore his power was especially great, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues sometimes learned of matters only afterward, and therefore his power was especially great, it is said.

sentences.zh: 論曰：光緒初元，复逢訓政，勵精圖治，宰輔多賢，頗有振興之象。

translations.literal: The historian comments: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign, regency was resumed and the court strove to govern well; many capable chief ministers served, and there was an air of revival.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign, with regency resumed, the court strove to govern well; capable ministers served, and there was an air of revival.

sentences.zh: 首輔文祥既逝，沈桂芬等承其遺風，以忠懇結主知，遇事能持之以正，雖無老成，尚有典型。

translations.literal: After chief minister Wen Xiang died, Shen Guifen and others inherited his legacy; with sincere earnestness they won the ruler's trust and could uphold principle in affairs; though lacking seasoned statesmanship, they still offered a model.
translations.idiomatic: After chief minister Wen Xiang died, Shen Guifen and others inherited his approach; with sincere earnestness they won the ruler's trust and upheld principle in affairs; though lacking seasoned statesmanship, they still offered a model.

sentences.zh: 及甲申法越、甲午日韓，外患內憂，國家多故。

translations.literal: By the jiashen Franco-Vietnamese conflict and the jiawu Japan-Korea crisis, foreign peril and domestic anxiety multiplied and the state faced many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: By the 1884 Sino-French conflict and the 1894 Japan-Korea crisis, foreign peril and domestic anxiety multiplied.

sentences.zh: 慈聖倦勤，經營園囿，稍事遊幸，而政紀亦漸弛矣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager grew weary of governing, devoted herself to gardens, and traveled somewhat for pleasure, and discipline in government gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager grew weary of governing, devoted herself to gardens and pleasure travel, and governmental discipline gradually slackened.

sentences.zh: 鴻藻久參樞密，眷遇獨隆。

translations.literal: Hongzao long participated in confidential council affairs and enjoyed uniquely lofty favor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzao long served on the Grand Council and enjoyed uniquely lofty favor.

sentences.zh: 桂芬以持重見賞，同龢以專斷致嫌。

translations.literal: Guifen was valued for his steadiness; Tonghe incurred dislike for his arbitrary decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen won praise for his steadiness, while Tonghe drew resentment for his tendency to decide matters on his own.

sentences.zh: 毓汶奔走其間，勤勞亦著，大體彌縫，賴以無事。

translations.literal: Yuwen bustled among them; his diligence was also notable, and by smoothing over the larger pattern affairs were kept without incident.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen bustled among them with conspicuous diligence, smoothing over larger disputes so that affairs remained largely untroubled.

sentences.zh: 然以政見異同，門戶之爭，牽及朝局，至數十年而未已。

translations.literal: Yet because of differences in political views and factional struggles, the court was drawn in, and this continued for several decades without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet differences in political views and factional rivalries drew in the court itself, and the strife continued for decades without end.

sentences.zh: 賢者之責，亦不能免焉。

translations.literal: Even men of worth could not escape this responsibility, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Even worthy men could not escape a share of the blame.
